subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Should OpenClaw ever replace result-bearing tool outputs such as `exec`, `read`, `web`, or `memory` with fixed model-visible placeholders for prefix-cache stability?
rationale: The code can preserve provider protocol pairing either way, but choosing which tool outputs the model may stop seeing is a product/runtime semantics decision that affects core agent correctness and cache cost.

options.title: Reject broad result-bearing placeholders
options.body: Require this PR to preserve actual outputs for result-bearing tools and use only a status-only or separately designed tool-result lifecycle policy.

options.title: Accept provider-level hiding
options.body: Maintainers may explicitly trade off agent reasoning fidelity for cache stability, but this should be documented and proven across affected tools/providers before merge.

options.title: Defer to the canonical issue
options.body: Pause or close this branch and resolve the linked issue through a narrower maintainer-approved design instead.

recommendation.title: Reject broad result-bearing placeholders
recommendation.body: Require this PR to preserve actual outputs for result-bearing tools and use only a status-only or separately designed tool-result lifecycle policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current-main history on the active provider conversion paths and is listed for Agents/Hooks ownership.
